A1.justification: Both complete, readable 14-page PDFs describe the same ME-POIs research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original experiments on Los Angeles and Houston mobility data, including benchmark results in Tables 1–4 and ablations in Table 5 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds training-duration experiments in Appendix A.4 and Figure 6.

M1.justification: The visit encoder, contrastive alignment, distribution transfer, auxiliary losses, and downstream prediction procedure are unchanged. Replacing ztext with zstatic in Sections 3.5–3.6 standardizes notation without changing the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Los Angeles and Houston datasets and five map-enrichment tasks. A.4 varies pretraining duration within existing Los Angeles coverage; it introduces no new dataset, task, or evaluation population.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–4 and Figure 4 is unchanged. Figure 6 plots only ME-POIs; its discussion references the existing mobility baselines without adding a comparison method.

E3.justification: New Appendix A.4 pretrains ME-POIs using 25%, 50%, and 75% of the Los Angeles observation year and evaluates opening hours and busyness against the full-duration reference. Existing splits, metrics, and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: A.4 and Figure 6 add a focused sensitivity analysis testing how shorter mobility histories affect representation quality on two tasks. The existing loss ablations and anchor-versus-sparse analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their five-run averaging statements, and existing error bars are unchanged. A.4 supplies no additional run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or uncertainty-estimation information.

E6.justification: Figure 6 adds reduced-duration results, including approximately 0.49 opening-hours F1 and 0.172 busyness MAE at 25% duration. Performance improves with longer histories; the full-duration endpoints match existing Table 3 results. Previously reported results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Appendix A.3 complexity analysis are substantively unchanged. The text-embedding symbol substitutions in Equations 16 and 18 introduce no new definition, reasoning, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about learning POI identity and function, addressing sparse visits, and improving map-enrichment performance. The duration study adds supporting evidence without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: A.4 newly interprets longer histories as capturing longitudinal and seasonal patterns while reducing transient noise. It also attributes effectiveness with shorter histories to aggregation into global POI prototypes. Existing interpretations and applicability statements remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Preprocessing, implementation, hyperparameters, hardware, prompt construction, and resource-access information are unchanged. Beyond the experimental duration settings assessed under E3, A.4 adds no implementation or window-selection instructions.

R1.justification: Section 5 and the cited-work set are unchanged. A.4 reuses the existing distinction between POI-centric and trajectory-centric learning; the bibliography only reflows after the added acknowledgments.

P1.justification: v3 adds Appendix A.4 and acknowledgments, updates the first author's affiliation and correspondence information, replaces the preprint notice with conference information, standardizes some notation, and corrects a typo. The main narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 6 with four metric plots grouped into two task panels on the final appendix page. Front-page details and reference layout change locally; existing figures and tables retain their displays and placement.

improvement.justification: A.4 adds useful evidence about sensitivity to available mobility history, which v2 did not directly test. The gain is limited by unspecified window selection and uncertainty reporting. Its broad baseline-superiority statement also needs qualification: at 25% duration, plotted busyness MAE is about 0.172 versus SKIP-GRAM's 0.171 in Table 3. Nevertheless, the added analysis modestly strengthens empirical understanding while preserving the existing method and evidence.
